states.name: Illinois

license.name: Alternative Retail Electric Supplier (ARES) certificate
license.security: Bond of $500,000 to serve all eligible customers, plus another $500,000 if marketing to homes in person (220 ILCS 5/16-115(d)(10))
license.review_time: ICC must grant or deny within 45 days after a complete application is filed and notice is published. It may extend that by up to 90 days for applicants seeking residential or small commercial customers (220 ILCS 5/16-115(b), (d)(6)).
license.fee: No ICC application fee (ICC ARES certification FAQ, revised Nov 17, 2025).
license.status_for_base: Base already holds ARES status in ComEd (per brief, not re-checked)

billing.summary: ComEd (PJM) is the target zone. Ameren Illinois is in MISO, not PJM.
billing.ComEd: Rider PORCB: ComEd buys supplier receivables and issues consolidated bills; tariff revised in 2026 (filing dated Mar 2, 2026)

filings.what: Annual kWh report: kWh sold to retail customers by utility territory, prior calendar year (83 Ill. Adm. Code 451.770)
filings.due: March 1 each year

filings.what: Annual managerial qualifications certification (451.750)
filings.due: During April each year

filings.what: Financial compliance items: ratings report or peak demand data, single billing estimate, insurance proof (451.740)
filings.due: April 1 to 30 each year

filings.what: Audited financial statements and accountant's report (451.740(e),(f))
filings.due: Within 120 days after fiscal year end

filings.what: Annual Section 16-115D(i) Compliance Report: certify no recovery of utility or IPA renewable costs from customers (83 Ill. Adm. Code 455.125)
filings.due: September 1 each year, for compliance year ending May 31

filings.what: Information ICC needs for the integrated resource plan under 16-201 (new duty under PA 104-0458)
filings.due: No fixed date: provide it when the ICC or the agencies ask, in the form requested (16-115A(a)(v), 16-201(e)). ICC staff's first plan is due Nov 15, 2026, the next Sept 30, 2029.

filings.what: Comply with any ICC resource procurement set under 16-111.5(b-10), a condition of ARES service
filings.due: No fixed date: applies only if the ICC approves a procurement under 16-111.5(b-10), which can start with the procurement plan for the delivery year beginning June 1, 2027.

consumer.rule: In-person sales: no visits before 9 a.m. or after 7 p.m. (earlier if dusk); photo ID badge with agent number and supplier name; Letter of Agency or third-party verification with agent out of earshot (83 Ill. Adm. Code 412.120)
Telemarketing, inbound calls, direct mail and online marketing rules (412.130 to 412.160); Uniform Disclosure Statement (412.115); rate notices (412.165); agent training (412.170)
Customer may rescind before enrollment is submitted or within 10 calendar days after the utility enrollment notice (412.210)
Residential and small commercial customers may end the contract at any time without termination fees; caps do not cover equipment or other services (412.220)
Respond in writing to an ICC-forwarded informal complaint within 14 days (412.320)

programs.name: Utility VPP program, 220 ILCS 5/16-107.9
programs.what: Utilities with over 300,000 customers must file VPP tariffs by Dec 31, 2027; ICC approves at least one per utility by Dec 31, 2028. Third-party aggregators (100 kW or more) can enroll customer or third-party owned batteries for upfront and performance payments.

programs.name: ComEd Rider SDVPP
programs.what: Scheduled Dispatch VPP under 220 ILCS 5/16-107.6(e) (not 16-107.9): pays enrolled storage for dispatch in peak windows. Filed June 1, 2026, effective July 16, 2026.

programs.name: Storage rebates, 220 ILCS 5/16-107.6 as amended by PA 104-0458
programs.what: Behind-the-meter storage rebate of $250 per kWh of nameplate capacity (stand-alone or paired); $300 per kWh base for storage paired with net-metering-eligible DG before the threshold date

programs.name: IPA storage procurement, 20 ILCS 3855/1-75(d-20)
programs.what: Initial procurement of at least 1,038 MW stand-alone storage (588 MW in PJM ComEd area); 3,000 MW cumulative by 2030. Utilities serving over 10,000 customers may not bid.

programs.name: Behind-the-meter interconnection
programs.what: 83 Ill. Adm. Code 466, Electric Interconnection of Distributed Generation Facilities (last amended May 26, 2022); covers limited-export and non-exporting DER (466.75). Storage not named in section titles.

dockets.id: ICC filing ERM #26-096 (no docket number shown on the filing)
dockets.what: ComEd Rider SDVPP tariff filed June 1, 2026 under PA 104-0458; ICC approval reported June 30, 2026 (secondary)

states.notes: Statute text read did not mention retail suppliers as VPP participants, only aggregators and direct participants. Base would likely enroll as an aggregator. No limit on utility-owned behind-the-meter storage found in the text read.

states.name: Pennsylvania

license.name: Electric Generation Supplier (EGS) license
license.rule: 52 Pa. Code Chapter 54, Subchapter D (54.31 to 54.43)
license.security: $250,000 initial; after year one, 10% of reported gross receipts (52 Pa. Code 54.40)
license.review_time: Protests are due within 15 days after newspaper notice is published. An unprotested complete application is processed within 45 days after the PUC accepts it, or it is deemed approved, unless a Secretarial Letter extends the review (52 Pa. Code 54.36, 54.37).
license.fee: Application fee $350, paid to Commonwealth of PA by certified check or money order; $350 for license amendments. Annual fee $350 plus a supplemental fee on gross intrastate revenues.

billing.summary: All four utilities offer consolidated utility billing and buy supplier receivables for basic supply; dual-billed accounts are excluded. PECO pays without discount and requires all residential accounts on consolidated billing to be in the program (tariff version effective Feb 20, 2024). PPL discounts 1.80% residential and 0.26% small C&I (Tariff 2S, effective July 1, 2026). Duquesne discounts 0.10% for residential and C&I under 300 kW, term June 1, 2025 to May 31, 2029. FirstEnergy PA covers residential and commercial schedules under Section 12.9 of Tariff S-1, with a clawback provision.
billing.FirstEnergy PA: PUC adopted a POR eligibility cap: only products priced at or below the price to compare at enrollment get POR, for contracts after June 1, 2027 (P-2026-3060298, secondary source)
billing.PPL: Proposal to make NITS nonbypassable would remove transmission from supplier prices (see dockets)

filings.what: Quarterly gross receipts report (52 Pa. Code 54.39(a))
filings.due: Within 30 days after each quarter ends

filings.what: Annual report for prior calendar year: tax info updates, gross receipts, kWh sold, fuel mix (54.39(b))
filings.due: April 30 each year

filings.what: Annual sales activity report on the PUC EGS form (54.203)
filings.due: April 30 each year

filings.what: Renew or replace financial security; security reset annually to 10% of gross receipts (54.40(d))
filings.due: At least 30 days before the security expires

filings.what: Annual $350 fee plus supplemental fee on gross intrastate revenues
filings.due: July 1 each year, paid by check.

filings.what: AEPS: hold alternative energy credits for the June 1 to May 31 reporting period (52 Pa. Code 75.61)
filings.due: 90-day true-up after May 31

consumer.rule: FirstEnergy PA default service order rejected a proposed ban on fixed-price residential auto-renewals (Oct 2026) (secondary)
Door-to-door: 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. (Oct to Mar) or 8 p.m. (Apr to Sep), supplier ID badge, leave copies of signed documents (52 Pa. Code 111.9)
Separate post-sale verification for door-to-door and phone sales; agent leaves the home before verification (111.7)
Disclosure statement: variable price conditions and limits, cancellation fees in dollars or formula; 3 business day rescission (54.5)
Expiration notices 45 to 60 days and at least 30 days before; silent fixed contract rolls to month-to-month or a fixed term cancellable without fees (54.10)

programs.name: Behind-the-meter interconnection
programs.what: 52 Pa. Code 75.21 to 75.40 (Chapter 75, Subchapter C). Small generator facility includes equipment that stores electricity (75.22).

programs.name: Residential storage incentive or third-party VPP
programs.what: No state home battery rebate or supplier-run VPP found. Act 129 Phase V plans (June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2031) filed by PPL and FirstEnergy PA add residential battery demand response run through the utility's own contractor; VPP bill HB 2264 passed the House June 16, 2026 and sits in a Senate committee.

dockets.what: PPL nonbypassable Customer Protection Transmission Rider (NITS moves off supplier bills), filed Sep 14, 2026, proposed start Q1 2028. Status active.
Base Retail, LLC comments asking for a supplier opt-out so it keeps NITS and its customers stay off the rider
FirstEnergy PA default service plan: POR limited to prices at or below the PTC from June 1, 2027

states.notes: POR price caps would hit a premium battery-bundled product hardest if priced above the price to compare. 52 Pa. Code 62.110 cited in the first pass is a natural gas rule and does not apply to EGSs.

states.name: New Jersey

license.agency: New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (BPU)
license.name: Third Party Supplier (TPS), electric power supplier license
license.security: $250,000 surety bond per electric power supplier license (N.J.A.C. 14:4-5.4(f))
license.review_time: No fixed decision deadline. Board staff must tell the applicant within 60 days if more information or investigation is needed, and the applicant then has 45 days to respond or the application is cancelled (N.J.A.C. 14:4-5.4(b), (c)).
license.fee: $350 nonrefundable application fee plus $1,500 initial license fee (refunded if denied); effective Sep 21, 2026

billing.summary: All four EDCs offer utility consolidated billing in which the utility assumes the supplier's undisputed commodity receivables (BPU Docket EO13030236). PSE&G and JCP&L pay the supplier by the 5th day after the bill due date; JCP&L moves a customer to dual billing when supplier charges are 120 days past due. Rockland Electric pays by the 20th day from the bill date and takes receivables at 100% of face value, with no discount. Atlantic City Electric offers the same billing with receivables assumed per BPU Staff (2013); its own supplier agreement and payment timing were not found.

filings.what: Annual Information Update Form with $750 nonrefundable fee (N.J.A.C. 14:4-5.12); file through the BPU External Access Portal from Nov 2, 2026
filings.due: Within 30 days before license anniversary date

filings.what: RPS annual report for the reporting year ending May 31, with ACP or SACP for any shortfall (N.J.A.C. 14:8-2.11)
filings.due: December 1 each year

consumer.rule: Telemarketing: FTC rules, no calls 9 p.m. to 8 a.m., honor do-not-call lists (N.J.A.C. 14:4-7.4; text as amended 2017, 2026 readoption not checked)

7-day rescission after the utility confirmation notice; variable price needs a clear formula; no price change without customer authorization; ETFs must be stated in the contract; no penalty on move, disability or death; 30 days notice before term ends, then month-to-month (14:4-7.6)

Residential and small commercial (50 kW or less) customers must get a one-page TPS Contract Summary in the Board's standard format, 12-point type, stating fixed or variable in bold, the term and the price per kWh; from Sep 21, 2026 it must also show residential customers the supplier's variable rates billed in the three preceding months (14:4-7.6A). A rate called fixed must state the fixed period and cannot be raised during it without the customer's affirmative consent, except as 14:4-7.6(l) allows (14:4-7.12).

programs.name: Garden State Energy Storage Program, Phase 2 Block 1
programs.what: Straw proposal (dated Aug 17, 2026) for up to 150 MW of residential behind-the-meter batteries, run by the four EDCs: $200 per kW-year of awarded capacity for 10 years, paid on performance in dispatch events (up to 35 a year, 4 hours each). Third-party owners and aggregators may enroll and must pass at least 70% of the incentive to the host customer. Customers on a third-party supply rate that passes through wholesale energy, capacity or transmission charges are not eligible.

programs.name: Utility-owned storage
programs.what: Atlantic City Electric petition (filed July 23, 2026) for a utility-owned BESS up to 500 MW, 4-hour, on ACE land in Salem County; Board retained it for hearing Sep 9, 2026

programs.name: Behind-the-meter interconnection
programs.what: N.J.A.C. 14:8-5; energy storage interconnection under 14:8-5.2(m) per a 2026 BPU request for information

dockets.what: QO22080540 is the GSESP docket for Phase 1 (Tranche 1 awards, Mar 4, 2026; secondary). Phase 2 Distributed Energy Storage Program has its own docket, QO26040116 (stakeholder notice dated Aug 17, 2026).
ACE 500 MW utility-owned battery petition and cost recovery; retained for hearing by the Board

states.notes: NJ is the strongest incentive opportunity if Phase 2 lets third-party owned home batteries in.

states.name: Maryland

license.name: Electricity supplier license
license.security: $250,000 bond for suppliers; $10,000 for brokers or aggregators only; $50,000 initial bond if taking deposits or prepayments
license.review_time: No fixed deadline in the rules. COMAR 20.51.02.09 says only that after review the Commission may grant a license if it will promote a competitive retail market.
license.term: No more than 3 years for new and renewed licenses (SB 1, 2024)

billing.summary: Utilities ended utility consolidated billing for residential supplier accounts and residential POR from Jan 1, 2026; residential suppliers must dual bill. PSC Order No. 92384 (Apr 28, 2026) approved the utilities' cessation plan. Proposed COMAR changes (May 2026) say utilities need not offer residential UCB after Dec 31, 2025 and cap supplier dual-billing late fees at 5% total.

filings.what: Annual update of changed application items; material changes within 30 days
filings.due: Within 120 days after supplier fiscal year end

filings.what: RPS Supplier Annual Report for prior calendar year (COMAR 20.61.04.02)
filings.due: April 1 each year (offshore wind items April 30)

filings.what: Marketed Renewable Electricity Sales Report (COMAR 20.61.04.01D)
filings.due: April 1 each year (offshore wind marketed sales April 30)

filings.what: Emissions and Fuel Mix Disclosure Report (PSC Order No. 77666)
filings.due: Annually by June 1 per a third-party compliance tracker; the PSC form lists it only as an annual report and Order No. 77666 was not found (secondary) (unverified)

filings.what: Deposit or prepayment bond: annual certification with the annual update, then quarterly reports
filings.due: With annual update; quarterly after

filings.what: PSC assessment (cap raised to 0.5% of gross operating revenue by SB 1)
filings.due: PSC sends the bill on or before May 1 each year; pay in full by the next July 15, or in four 25% installments on the 15th of July, October, January and April (Public Utilities Article 2-110(c)).

consumer.rule: SB 1 (2024), agreements from Jan 1, 2025: residential non-green price may not exceed the trailing 12-month average utility SOS rate at signing
Residential terms up to 12 months; auto-renewal only with notices 90 and 30 days before; green power may not auto-renew
No variable rates except seasonal changes up to twice a year; time-of-use rates allowed
Green power needs at least the greater of 51% or RPS plus 1%; PSC sets a general price cap, supplier-specific price generally up to 150% of it
Utilities may not buy residential supplier receivables; no commissions to energy salespersons for enrollments
Energy salesperson licensing from July 1, 2025; supplier penalties up to $25,000
Telephone solicitation only 8 a.m. to 9 p.m.; license number on marketing materials (COMAR 20.53.07.07)
Door-to-door: ID badge, business card with license number, leave copies of signed documents, leave when asked (COMAR 20.53.10.06)

programs.name: Statutory storage target, utility procurement
programs.what: Pepco and Delmarva propose 29 MW utility-owned front-of-meter storage; Phase 1 procured 14.5 MW third-party owned (30% third-party share, Order No. 91705). BGE proposes 42 MW utility-owned (40 MW at C&I customer sites) plus 16 MW third-party via Index Storage Credit. (secondary)

programs.name: Behind-the-meter interconnection
programs.what: COMAR 20.50.09, Small Generator Facility Interconnection Standards (Levels 1 to 4). Storage treatment in the text not read this pass.

programs.name: Residential storage incentive or VPP open to third parties
programs.what: Maryland Energy Administration Residential and Commercial Energy Storage rebate: FY27 round open until May 31, 2027 (about $4 million); the FY26 terms paid 30% of installed cost up to $5,000 per home, and third-party owners of the battery could apply. Separately, the PSC approved two-year DRIVE Act virtual power plant pilots in Case No. 9761 (June 2026), including aggregator pathways at BGE and Potomac Edison and about $300 per kW-year for home batteries; the order text was not opened (secondary)

dockets.what: Utility storage procurement phases, including utility-owned BGE, Pepco and Delmarva proposals (secondary)

dockets.id: PC 65 (Order No. 91463, Dec 30, 2024; Order No. 92384, Apr 28, 2026)
dockets.what: Ends residential POR and residential utility consolidated billing from Jan 1, 2026

dockets.id: Proposed COMAR 20.53.05 and new 20.53.07.16 (May 2026, RM number not shown)
dockets.what: Draft rules: no required residential UCB after Dec 31, 2025; dual-billing late fees 1.5% steps, 5% total cap

states.notes: Hardest residential market in PJM for a premium product: SOS price cap, no POR, no residential utility consolidated billing (dual billing only), near-ban on variable rates. Time-of-use is the allowed exception.

states.name: Delaware

license.name: Electric supplier certificate
license.security: Copy of any performance bond required by the utility service agreement (2.2.15); a bond, if required, is $10,000 (2.3.3.3)
license.review_time: No fixed deadline. The applicant publishes notice, staff makes a recommendation after the comment period closes, and the Commission then approves, conditions or denies; an application can be rejected if the applicant leaves a staff request unanswered for 4 months (3001 sections 2.6, 2.8, 2.10).

billing.summary: Delmarva Power is the only investor-owned EDC and POR is in place. When a supplier uses Delmarva consolidated billing, Delmarva buys its commodity receivables (not early termination fees or non-commodity charges) under the PSC order in Docket 15-1693 and pays undisputed charges by the 5th day after the bill due date. The residential discount rate was 4.9155% and 0% for other classes effective June 1, 2023; later updates were not checked.

filings.what: Supplier information update to PSC and DPA (12.3)
filings.due: Within 30 days of a change and annually by April 30

filings.what: Green power product compliance report with VREC retirement evidence (13.4), only if offering green power
filings.due: Within 120 days after end of compliance year

filings.what: RPS: no supplier compliance report; only Delmarva files an RPS compliance report (within 120 days of compliance year end) and recovers RPS cost from all customers
filings.due: Not applicable to suppliers

consumer.rule: Telemarketing and door-to-door rules (3001 sections 11.7 and 11.8)
Contract summary and variable rate disclosure (sections 6.2, 6.3)
No early cancellation fee on the commodity part of a variable price contract (6.2.2.12.4)
Residential rescission within 3 business days (6.2.2.7.1)

2026 amendments: variable rate notice 12 days before billing period close, PA-style fixed rate renewal notices, not-the-utility statement, voicemail script, written enrollment notice within 7 days (secondary)

programs.name: Utility-owned storage
programs.what: Delaware allows Exelon utilities to own storage for resiliency (Exelon CFO, secondary)

programs.name: Behind-the-meter interconnection and storage incentives
programs.what: DNREC Solar + Storage Pilot (effective Aug 11, 2026): $250 per kWh up to $6,000 for a home battery, capped at 50% of cost, Delmarva customers only. The battery must be bought and owned by the homeowner and enrolled in a Delmarva active dispatch program for 10 years, so third-party owned batteries do not qualify. Delmarva also asked the PSC to approve a Bring Your Own Battery pilot (Docket 25-1554, filed Dec 9, 2025); approval status not confirmed.

states.notes: Small market, single EDC. Cheapest license fee path but limited scale.

states.name: Ohio

license.name: Competitive Retail Electric Service (CRES) provider certificate
license.security: Financial assurance set by each utility's supplier tariff (4901:1-10-29), not a fixed PUCO bond
license.review_time: Deemed approved 30 days after filing unless PUCO suspends; then decision within 90 days of suspension (R.C. 4928.08)
license.fee: No PUCO application fee is listed in the CRES application form and filing instructions (04-2023). Certified providers pay annual assessments under R.C. 4905.10 and 4911.18.
license.term: Certificate renews every two years; renewal filed 30 to 90 days before expiration

billing.summary: AEP Ohio, AES Ohio and FirstEnergy Ohio do not buy supplier receivables: each offers rate-ready and bill-ready consolidated billing and forwards customer payments by posting priority (AES Ohio FAQ; FirstEnergy Ohio FAQ dated July 2018; AEP Ohio handbook July 2024 shows no receivables program). Duke Energy Ohio's supplier tariff allows a voluntary agreement for Duke to buy supplier receivables.

filings.what: Annual RPS compliance report
filings.due: April 15 each year

filings.what: Annual report for fiscal assessment (CRES providers included; 2025 report under Case 26-0001-AU-RPT)
filings.due: April 30 (2026 deadline); 50% initial payment by June 20 if over $1,000; final assessment by November 1

filings.what: Certificate renewal
filings.due: Every two years, 30 to 90 days before expiration

consumer.rule: Door-to-door: background checks, photo ID, hours 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. absent local rules (4901:1-21-05)
Third-party verification for door-to-door sales; recorded verification for phone enrollment (4901:1-21-06)
Variable rate contracts need an index formula or a factor explanation; no early termination fee if using the factor explanation (4901:1-21-12)
Seven-day rescission after the utility confirmation notice (4901:1-21-11)

programs.name: Behind-the-meter interconnection
programs.what: Ohio Adm.Code 4901:1-22, Interconnection Services; most rules amended effective July 20, 2026; definitions (4901:1-22-01) address energy storage

programs.name: Residential storage incentive or third-party VPP
programs.what: None found. Checked PUCO supplier pages, the AEP Ohio CRES handbook, the CESA VPP program table (updated Aug 2026, no Ohio rows) and bill searches; the only residential demand response seen is AEP Ohio's smart thermostat program, and HB 427 is still a bill (secondary)

dockets.what: Financial security now tied to utility tariffs

states.notes: Large shopping market with clear rules. Collateral is negotiated utility by utility.

license.name: Electricity Supplier License
license.security: Integrity bond $50,000 if applicant cannot meet financial standards ($10,000 for non-title aggregators or brokers) (4605.2); Customer Payments Bond $50,000 before taking deposits or prepayments (4604.2)
license.review_time: Decision within 15 days after application deemed complete (4602.6)
license.term: Valid until revoked or surrendered; reviewed every 5 years (4602.7)

billing.summary: Pepco buys supplier receivables under its Electric Supplier Coordination Tariff (POR Supplier Discount Rate, Schedule 3). A 2026 discount rate true-up is pending in PEPPOR-2026-01 after Order No. 22883 (June 12, 2026).

filings.due: Every 5 years from issue or last review

filings.what: Customer Payments Bond certification if taking deposits (15 DCMR 4604.2)

filings.what: Update application information (4607.1)
filings.due: Within 30 days of a change

filings.what: Electricity Supplier Education Workshop (4603.1)

filings.due: March 25 of the year after the compliance year

filings.what: RPS compliance fee payment, if any
filings.due: Between October 1 and November 1

consumer.rule: Home solicitation only 9 a.m. to sunset, photo ID naming the agent and supplier (15 DCMR 327.23)
Phone sales: independent third-party verification or recording; written contract sent within 5 business days; enroll only after rescission ends (327.17 to 327.19)
3 business day rescission (327.21)
Notify PSC 3 business days before first marketing; door-to-door agents show photo ID (4602.8)

Offers may be fixed or variable, and a variable offer must say the rate may follow market conditions and may end up higher or lower than an introductory rate (327.7(c)). The contract must state the amount of any early cancellation fee and the renewal procedure; the rule sets no fee cap. Written notice is required 35 days before a contract expires (327.44) and 45 days before any renewal, with rate changes highlighted and, for automatic renewals, how to cancel without penalty (327.45).

programs.name: Behind-the-meter interconnection
programs.what: 15 DCMR Chapter 40 Small Generator Interconnection Rules, up to 20 MW; non-exporting storage load treated as customer load (4008.16); exporting front-of-meter storage goes to Level 4 (4008.19)

DOEE issued a July 2026 request for information on batteries of 100 kW to 30 MW, not an incentive.
